incident-bot: P1 ALERT — suspicious auth egress detected from auth-proxy cluster to multiple external IPs. Auto-runbook started: https://redwood.runbook/sus-auth-egress :rotating_light:

alex (eng-oncall): taking it. I saw the pager, looking at logs now.

priya (sec-oncall): oncall here. initial question: is this internal test traffic or likely exfil? :eyes:

maria (ops-lead): from quick glance it's real traffic hitting /auth/validate with valid tokens, high fanout to external endpoint 198.51.100.42. Could be a forwarded log or an upstream misconfig.

raj (backend): looks like the forwarding lambda has been folding batched auth debug payloads to an external bucket — suspecting misrouted forwarder config. sample log:
```
2026-03-18T12:03:10Z auth-proxy svc=auth-proxy req_id=abc123 path=/auth/validate status=200 user_id=uid_789 token="[REDACTED]" forward_to=s3://auth-debug-exports/external/2026-03-18/part-0001.json
```

alex (eng-oncall): thanks. if forwarder is staging-facing but target bucket was misconfigured to public/external, we need to stop it ASAP.

priya (sec-oncall): immediate actions: 1) block external IPs from cluster egress via WAF/security-groups; 2) disable forwarding lambda; 3) rotate any exposed service account keys. I'll coordinate 1+2 now.

tom (infra): putting automated WAF block on 198.51.100.0/24 now. applying security group egress deny to auth-proxy-nodes.

sam (support-lead): heads-up for customers: we should prepare a short internal note. Do we have confirmed data exfil?

maria (ops-lead): not yet confirmed customer PII exposed. The forwarder was exporting debug logs that may contain token fragments. We'll treat as potential credential exposure.

alice (support): prepping a proactive support blurb if we need to notify customers. ETA 20m for draft.

raj (backend): disabling the forwarder config on prod: `kubectl -n infra set env deploy/debug-forwarder ENABLE=false --record` — patching now.

alex (eng-oncall): good. after disable, we should rotate the IAM keys for svc-auth-forwarder and revoke sessions created by those keys. Priya, can you own key rotation?

priya (sec-oncall): will handle key rotation. Plan: create new key pair, update forwarder secret, revoke old key. Est. 25-40 minutes. Notifying IAM team to expedite.

jules (legal): please preserve all artifacts and logs. Legal wants a timeline and scope once we have confirmed which objects were sent externally. Do not delete anything.

maria (ops-lead): confirmed — do not delete. we'll snapshot the S3 prefix and bucket ACLs for forensics.

tom (infra): snapshot done. bucket: auth-debug-exports, path external/2026-03-18/. Downloaded a redacted sample to secure forensic storage.

priya (sec-oncall): running quick grep for token patterns across exported objects. If tokens present, we will trigger forced session expiry for affected tokens and rotate keys.

alex (eng-oncall): command to invalidate sessions: `POST /internal/sessions/invalidate-batch {"subject_ids": [...]}` — raj can run once we have list.

raj (backend): standing by. I can run an invalidate for the affected user_ids. Need list from priya.

priya (sec-oncall): found ~1200 objects with traces; sampling 100 objects — rough estimate: ~0.01% of active sessions might have token fragments. Not all are usable.

sam (support-lead): customer impact note: small fraction of users may be forced to re-login if we invalidate sessions. We recommend we communicate proactively only if confirmed compromise.

alice (support): draft ready: short notification describing token rotation and forced re-login for a subset of users. Hold until scope confirmed.

maria (ops-lead): escalation: SRE to stand by for rollback if front-end errors spike after session invalidation. Alex, coordinate with SRE.

alex (eng-oncall): pinging #eng-sre for a short window starting t+30m.

priya (sec-oncall): executing key rotation now. Steps: 1) create new key for svc-auth-forwarder; 2) update secret in k8s; 3) disable old key in IAM; 4) rotate tokens and revoke sessions if sample shows usable tokens.

raj (backend): after rotation, I'll run the invalidate batch for the 4k session ids we pulled from objects. Will throttle to avoid login storms.

tom (infra): monitoring network egress and WAF blocks. all egress to 198.51.100.0/24 currently blocked.

jules (legal): also confirm if any customer-controlled buckets were involved. If so, legal needs their list for notification timelines.

priya (sec-oncall): no customer buckets detected yet — only our debug bucket.

maria (ops-lead): action checklist: 1) block egress (done), 2) disable forwarder (done), 3) rotate keys (in progress), 4) snapshot artifacts (done), 5) run session invalidation (pending), 6) draft customer comms (drafted).

sam (support-lead): support on standby for inbound tickets. We'll prepare templates.

alex (eng-oncall): running a small invalidate now for 200 sessions as a canary. Raj, watch auth metrics for 5-10m.

raj (backend): canary invalidate executed. auth error rate + latent login surge within expected bounds. standing by.

priya (sec-oncall): rotation complete, old key disabled. collecting final scope report.

maria (ops-lead): sec confirms scope ~= 0.01% sessions affected, no known PII in sampled objects. recommend internal SEV -> P1 resolved -> followup incident review.

jules (legal): proceed with internal timeline. no customer notification required at this time per current scope, but hold onto comms templates if scope increases.

alice (support): saving draft and ready to send if we escalate.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — mitigations applied. status: containment in place, key rotation complete, forensics collection ongoing. See runbook: https://redwood.runbook/sus-auth-egress

maria (ops-lead): handing off to postmortem channel #postmortems-incidents. Follow-up owner: priya (sec-oncall) for forensic report and raj for remediation doc.

priya (sec-oncall): will own the forensic report. target ETA initial report 4 hours.

alex (eng-oncall): thanks team. closing live bridge. we'll reconvene if new evidence. :white_check_mark:
